name.description: The session's display label. NOT unique and not an identifier: several sessions may legitimately share one, and the id remains the identity. Set by POST /v1/sessions or PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}; when unset, derived from the session's first non-retracted prompt, normalised to one line and cut at 80 runes. name_source says which of the two this is.

name_source.description: Where `name` came from. `operator` is a label a human typed; `derived` is a cut of the session's first prompt and is NOT something anyone chose; `none` means the session has neither a label nor a prompt to derive one from, and `name` is empty. A screen offering a rename affordance needs the distinction — presenting a derived cut as the session's name is a claim nobody made.

agents.description: The DISTINCT agent-profile names this session's RUNS pinned, sorted. Deliberately plural: there is no session-to-agent association in this system — a run pins an agent revision, so a session may have used none, one, or several — and a screen that labels this column 'Agent' singular is asserting something the data does not say. Empty for a session whose runs pinned no agent profile, which includes every run pinned to a run template: a template carries executable config but must not impersonate an agent identity.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens METERED for this session, summed from the usage ledger. This is not a provider invoice and can be lower than one: the tokens of a model step aborted mid-stream by an interrupt never reach the ledger, because the provider's counts ride a final stream chunk a canceled stream never receives. On a session whose steps were interrupted, treat this as a floor.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens METERED for this session, summed from the usage ledger. Same floor caveat as input_tokens.

first_activity_at.description: When this session's earliest run was created, or null when it has never run. Null is a session with no duration, not one lasting zero.

last_activity_at.description: When this session's latest run last CHANGED STATE, or null when it has never run. On a session with a run still in flight this is the last transition and not the present moment, so it is not 'now' — elapsed time for a live session is the reader's own clock minus first_activity_at.

duration_ms.description: last_activity_at minus first_activity_at in milliseconds, or null when the session has never run. It spans RECORDED activity: for a session still running it is the span so far between transitions, not wall-clock elapsed.

auto_approve_tools.description: Whether this session decides its own gated TOOL calls through the standing authorization an operator armed, instead of parking the run for a human each time (E30 T1, migration 000056). It is on the projection because an operator must be able to SEE from the screen that a session is answering its own approvals — a switch whose state is visible only to the code that reads it is a switch nobody can audit from outside. False for every session that never armed it, which is every session created before the field existed.

auto_approve_publications.description: Whether this session decides its own PUBLICATIONS — pushes, pull requests, merges — through the standing authorization. SEPARATE from auto_approve_tools, and the screen must render the two separately, because they are not the same risk: a gated tool call's effects land in the run's own workspace while an operator watches, and a publication writes to somebody's repository and outlives the session. A screen that showed one 'auto-approve: on' badge for both would be telling an operator something false about the second.

auto_approve_set_by.description: The principal whose standing authorization decides this session's approvals — the human who armed it, stamped server-side from the verified key. It is NOT decoration: the auto-decision is made AS this principal and still passes the project's `approvers` policy for them, so an armed session grants exactly what that person could have granted by clicking. Empty when nothing was ever armed, and empty means unidentified, which a project WITH an approver list refuses.

auto_approve_set_at.description: When the standing authorization was last armed, or null when neither half is armed — so 'armed at' never outlives the arming.
